The importance of the 2026 election is obvious. A dictatorial president subverting the Constitution to gain more power for himself while Congress stands by in thrall, subservient to his political movement. November may be our last chance to stand and defend our democracy and our elections.
Pitch in $35 -- right now -- to fuel our efforts to inform eligible voters, get them registered, get their ballot cast, and make every vote count >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=071926_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
When it comes to fighting voter suppression, our work is never done. Increasing participation in free and fair elections that are accessible to ALL eligible voters is our #1 goal for 2026, Team.
Unfortunately, this is what we're facing as we start the year:
➜ Mail-in voting is under threat in state legislatures and now from the Supreme Court.
➜ Without vote-by-mail, millions of Americans will not be able to vote.
➜ With the 2026 midterm election around the corner, this is a disaster.
Remember, Team: Attacks on mail-in voting are voter suppression, plain and simple. We need your help now, more than ever. Will you chip in $35 to protect vote-by-mail before it’s too late? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=071926_3&amount=35]

These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

But NVIDIA isn’t the only one who needs it.

Elon Musk’s SpaceX builds on it — their job postings demand experience with this firm’s technology, in writing.

Jeff Bezos builds Amazon’s AI chips on it, and Blue Origin runs its control systems on it. Apple, Google, Meta, Samsung, and Qualcomm all pay it billions in royalties every year.

Its technology is already in the phone in your hand.

Every time you open an app, stream a video, or ask your assistant a question, [_this company’s_](https://links.notify.powerfieldnotes.com/u/click?_t=e11a13a19fbf4d1ab3d90eea26ea896f&_m=3e424b3752314259bdcce6f9ec917c05&_e=Nbmz3bjXx_uhaHDCpMeVhrUy4waW2ONkQ99IGCFgszfWLPdEQMCTemFj2sjmLoTEdA6GHTxctF-kXtkueAjTacGBDD0DXmr6gsHP1l92adIRTgwsJjuR3v22Ia3dgZGQO3Ayr96G7DLP5CC9mXMt4E0NeJsNcBfL5C2EuYydJDuNMUOTdiozgzlodaTFt46-rddzbbSOJJvCpBPi9saVqyY6zF6Frtwroqs-3-RHbswRFIT0Dhhrl0p0cuVI63eE-PMKq6O2o6uvxRHlJtUGaFe3T5gbIX2tSiqelEqUnx0Sy-rjG9YUmT_4zHUJJVWmC1pxneeB5vmwaGwIxAEAc3zoRiTPzZeddx3RtO-iQlUDFeUvSnXlGAJhSTPMuaqgziDMIxpCl49J6ZZG6WQgxq1V_7xpCERG5NmngDl72ko9_67bGPRzwLmp9r82omk3LCQ7bImCkMa7BgC_s09hqWm7aYQZrz72Ae3sMRDIWw4%3D) architecture is running underneath.

| | **Q2 2026 Was the Worst Quarter for Oil Markets Since COVID. US Petroleum Markets Are the Story. Iranian Power Infrastructure Is Now a Casualty. Here Is the Week's Full Accounting.**
---
| | EIA's Today in Energy documented Q2 2026 petroleum markets: they were "characterized by continued disruptions to international crude oil and petroleum product flows through the Strait of Hormuz, contributing to higher and more volatile crude oil prices through most of the quarter." International buyers sought alternative supply sources for petroleum products — directly driving up US petroleum product exports to record levels. Cushing, Oklahoma storage — the delivery point for WTI futures — fell below 20 million barrels during the week ending June 19 through July 10, the lowest sustained inventory in years. The EIA's July indicator table puts the full picture in one row: Brent spot averaged $82/barrel in 2026 in their forecast versus $69 in 2025 — a $13/barrel average increase for the year, representing the largest annual crude price increase since 2021-2022.
---
| | Iran's Energy Ministry called on Iranians this week to limit air conditioning use after US strikes damaged power lines near Bandar Abbas, causing electricity supply disruptions in southern Iran, per CNN. This is the first documented case in the conflict of US strikes directly degrading a civilian electricity supply system. Trump threatened in his national address to strike Iranian "electric generating plants" if Iran does not negotiate — which would be a far more complete destruction of civilian power infrastructure than the incidental damage that has already occurred. Iran processes approximately 90% of its oil exports through Kharg Island; it generates significant electricity from natural gas infrastructure in the south. Targeting either at full scale would cause cascading civilian harm that humanitarian law experts say constitutes a war crime. The line between military infrastructure and civilian power in Iran's case is thin. The strikes are moving closer to it.

Dear Friends,I wanted you to be among the first to hear the news—I am excited to announce that I’m running for Daly City Council!This campaign is built on one simple principle: local government should provide **opportunity for all.** Today, families across our city are feeling the squeeze of rising housing, healthcare, and grocery costs. Young families wonder if they can afford to stay, and seniors worry about being priced out. Working people deserve a City Hall focused on making life more affordable while protecting the unique quality of life that makes Daly City so special.As a lifelong resident and the proud son of working-class Filipino immigrants, these challenges are personal. My family has called Daly City home since 1977, when my parents bought our home at the Top of the Hill. I attended our local schools and learned the values of hard work, service, and looking out for your neighbors.My career has been dedicated to serving this community. For the past ten years, I’ve served as Chief of Staff to San Mateo County Supervisor David J. Canepa. As Vice Chair of Daly City's Personnel Board, I’ve also gained firsthand experience in making local government more responsive and accountable. I know how to navigate government, build partnerships, and bring resources home because I’ve spent my career doing exactly that.If elected, I will focus on delivering real results that provides opportunity for all:
* **Affordability:** Improving housing affordability, expanding healthcare access, and helping families keep up with the cost of living.
* **Public Safety & Infrastructure:** Investing in first responders, fixing flooding challenges, repairing potholes, and strengthening transit options.
* **Family Support:** Advocating for a childcare center at Daly City Hall to support working parents and make city services more accessible.
* **Senior Care:** Protecting and expanding programs that help seniors age safely and independently in their homes.

**I’m ready to step into a leadership role myself in every way but I can’t do it without you. As I know from helping to run Supervisor Canepa’s campaigns and you probably do too, campaigns are not cheap.**[**Can you be one of my founding donors?**](https://us.list-manage.com/AKOXwIpqEUE?e=a77f0ac4a9&c2id=f2f0b537fa844d5b5a30cd2c82e303f0)**Nothing is more important to a campaign than early money, as it helps us get off to a fast start and build a winning campaign from the get-go.**
[**Could you donate today in any amount up to $5,900? $1,000, $500, $100 or even $25 will make a huge difference to my campaign at this early stage.**](https://us.list-manage.com/9O8DEOWxsMt?e=a77f0ac4a9&c2id=f2f0b537fa844d5b5a30cd2c82e303f0)
Our city has always been defined by hardworking families, diverse neighborhoods, and neighbors who care about one another. Together, we can build a Daly City that is more affordable, safer, better prepared for the future, and continues to be a place where families of every generation can thrive – a Daly City that truly provides opportunity for all.I would be honored to earn your support, your ideas, and your vote.In friendship,
Tony BayudanCandidate for Daly City Council**P.S. Anything you can donate today at**[**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tony-bayudan-1**](https://us.list-manage.com/17nY9h13TgY?e=a77f0ac4a9&c2id=f2f0b537fa844d5b5a30cd2c82e303f0)**will be so valuable – even if it’s just $5!**

Sustainer Sunday
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260719-3054)
Peter,
Every Sunday, we share the story of someone who's helping build this movement and why they believe Fran is the leader Wisconsin needs.
Earlier this year, Fran earned an endorsement from [Black Leaders Organizing for Communities (BLOC)](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16816?t=1&akid=3054%2E105371%2ESDLgXR), the powerhouse grassroots organization that organizes year-round in Milwaukee's Black communities.
Today, we're hearing from Angela Lang, BLOC's founder and executive director, on why she’s backing Fran.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260719.6pD6zH&refcode=em20260719-3054&t=2&akid=3054%2E105371%2ESDLgXR)
* * *
_Fran has been authentically showing up in our communities for years, not just when she is running for office._
_She doesn’t shy away from tough conversations. She listens, speaks honestly and is committed to being accountable to the people she serves._
_Wisconsinites have been waiting for leaders willing to challenge a status quo that has failed working people for far too long._
_Fran understands that real change begins by listening to the people most affected and then having the courage to fight alongside them._
_\- Angela Lang, Milwaukee_
* * *
Angela’s testimonial reflects what this campaign hears every day across Wisconsin: People are ready for leadership that does not take their communities for granted.
Trust can't be bought – not with corporate PAC money, not with a billionaire's checkbook. It's earned door by door, block by block, conversation by conversation. That's how Fran has run this campaign, and it's how she'll lead as governor. But out-organizing candidates with establishment backing takes resources.

Team Hong

subject: I brought my son to the auto shop because we couldn't find childcare
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY MGP VICTORY FUND, A JOINT
body:

Before I was sworn into Congress, my husband and I brought our son to our auto repair shop most days.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
Not because it was cute. Because there was no other option.
There wasn't a daycare within a reasonable drive, and the care we could find cost more than we could afford. So he came to work with us — in a shop full of lifts and tools — because that was the choice in front of us.
We are not unusual. That's the reality for working parents across Southwest Washington, especially in our rural communities, where you can drive an hour and still not find an open spot.
Here's something almost no one in DC will say out loud: out of 535 members of Congress, only six of the women have a child under six. I'm one of them. Most of the people writing childcare policy haven't had to find a daycare spot — or afford one — in decades. I still do.
I didn't need a briefing to understand this problem. I lived it.
That's why I introduced the Expanding Childcare in Rural America Act . And it's why I spent three years on something so basic it sounds made up: in Washington State, red tape makes it easier for a home daycare to hand a kid a processed, packaged snack than to peel a banana or cut up an apple.
This spring, the House finally passed my bill to cut that red tape. It's a small thing that makes smaller daycares stay afloat, which are lifelines for working families.
That's the work I came here to do: fixing the specific, stupid problems that make it harder to raise a family and earn a living.
But I'm one of the most targeted Democrats in the country, in one of the closest districts in America. Donald Trump has endorsed my opponent, and national Republicans will spend whatever it takes to take this seat back.
Will you chip in $5, $10, or whatever you can to keep this campaign going? Every dollar helps us reach one more working parent who's tired of being told their problems aren't worth solving. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
Thank you for standing with me.
—Marie

subject: You can’t pour from an empty cup
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Sara Jacobs for Congress
body:

Friends [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50] ,
Right now, so much of what’s going on feels hard. And if you’re anything like me, there are far too many things keeping you up at night. That’s our reality right now, and I’m not going to write you an email pretending everything is all sunshine and rainbows.
I’ve also been thinking a lot lately about the fights ahead, and about how important it is to make time for the things that bring us joy. Even in the middle of all of this — or rather, especially in the middle of all of this!
I’m a proud aunt, and I take aunt-ing very seriously — to the point of reading toddler blogs in my spare time. One of the main takeaways from the blogs I follow is that you can't pour from an empty cup . In other words, if we're going to keep showing up as the best version of ourselves (whether as an aunt, a friend, a Congresswoman, or whatever else life brings), we have to take care of ourselves first.
I took a few days off recently for the first time in a very long time — and if you’re in the position to do the same, I hope you will. But at the very least, consider this email your reminder to make time for yourself in small ways: Move your body. Cook something delicious. Get some sunshine. Play pickleball (my personal stress reliever). Go for a walk. Listen to a podcast. Read a book!
And if you're looking for something to read, I've got some recommendations. Here are some of my favorites from this summer:
Into the Blue by Emma Brodie — 9/10. A little weird, but it kept my attention and had some great plot twists.
The Night We Met by Abby Jimenez — 8/10. The perfect light beach read. Very sweet.
Traitor to His Class by H.W. Brands — 9/10. OK, this is a biography of FDR that somehow isn't boring at all. Full of fascinating details — like the fact that his mother Sara's (a fellow no-H Sara!) family is from New Bedford, just like mine.
The Shippers by Katherine Center — 8/10. Perfectly light and cute.
And honestly, anything by Emily Henry, because you can't go wrong!
If you’re reading something good right now, I'd love to hear about it — so please reply to this email and tell me what you’re enjoying, or what’s in your to-be-read pile. I'm always looking for my next book.
Take care of yourselves. We need you in this fight for the long haul!
—Sara

clean_body: [] Friends [] , Right now, so much of what’s going on feels hard. And if you’re anything like me, there are far too many things keeping you up at night. That’s our reality right now, and I’m not going to write you an email pretending everything is all sunshine and rainbows. I’ve also been thinking a lot lately about the fights ahead, and about how important it is to make time for the things that bring us joy. Even in the middle of all of this — or rather, especially in the middle of all of this! I’m a proud aunt, and I take aunt-ing very seriously — to the point of reading toddler blogs in my spare time. One of the main takeaways from the blogs I follow is that you can't pour from an empty cup . In other words, if we're going to keep showing up as the best version of ourselves (whether as an aunt, a friend, a Congresswoman, or whatever else life brings), we have to take care of ourselves first. I took a few days off recently for the first time in a very long time — and if you’re in the position to do the same, I hope you will. But at the very least, consider this email your reminder to make time for yourself in small ways: Move your body. Cook something delicious. Get some sunshine. Play pickleball (my personal stress reliever). Go for a walk. Listen to a podcast. Read a book! And if you're looking for something to read, I've got some recommendations. Here are some of my favorites from this summer: Into the Blue by Emma Brodie — 9/10. A little weird, but it kept my attention and had some great plot twists. The Night We Met by Abby Jimenez — 8/10. The perfect light beach read. Very sweet. Traitor to His Class by H.W. Brands — 9/10. OK, this is a biography of FDR that somehow isn't boring at all. Full of fascinating details — like the fact that his mother Sara's (a fellow no-H Sara!) family is from New Bedford, just like mine. The Shippers by Katherine Center — 8/10. Perfectly light and cute. And honestly, anything by Emily Henry, because you can't go wrong! If you’re reading something good right now, I'd love to hear about it — so please reply to this email and tell me what you’re enjoying, or what’s in your to-be-read pile. I'm always looking for my next book. Take care of yourselves. We need you in this fight for the long haul! —Sara [] Congresswoman Sara Jacobs California’s 51st District CONTRIBUTE NOW [] [] Paid for by Sara Jacobs for Congress Sara Jacobs for Congress PO Box 120085 San Diego, CA 92112 United States www.facebook.com/SaraJacobsCA/ [www.facebook.com/SaraJacobsCA/] twitter.com/sarajacobsca [twitter.com/sarajacobsca] www.instagram.com/sarajacobsca/ [www.instagram.com/sarajacobsca/] We believe these emails are a critical way for Sara to stay in touch with supporters and constituents. ## Spain Beats Argentina 1-0 for World Cup Title
Spain's Ferran Torres scored in the 106th minute to lift his country to a [1-0 victory over Argentina](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO5CAQRL_Gzhg1PQzYAcElm-2lF1o90B73CYMF7Fr79yfPL1xWpZJK9erP5_JJkiS_ftPOvq9lyXy2xL1zXdpBkk_J7Sw1hq-jndLDxpEWBLQKnEJYIkn6WcwY_cqMfB_ZazeZh9EzmnHzpIFWi9P0vGtDFpF1XHUE1BaDm2kUf7WBQ9AAD9Q31pMJOEd4kHYTPAYDHKWXevtbJPeN1_RTvrneQtnH5Lfejzbcfw34MeAHHRfAFV2mdgmJ3-rFuUsm9YZSZ6kpqvB1qFUyJdVCqax2bk3UGkJAS6QxzoiW7T2CfVrQT-fAajdWH49TUpJm3WDgtZOk95j-Xw9-e_wXAAD__10vg_o) and its second World Cup title. The dramatic finish capped a record-setting FIFA World Cup that drew more than 6.6 million fans to 16 stadiums across the U.S., Canada, and Mexico. ---
| | Brent crude rose 3% Sunday to $90.78 per barrel — its highest level since the April 2026 war peak — after the US struck nine Iranian cities in its ninth consecutive night of operations and Iran hit the Jordanian city of Aqaba. WTI crude is now up 24.89% year-on-year, per Trading Economics. The EIA's July STEO, completed July 1, forecast Q3 2026 Brent at $74/barrel and US retail gasoline at $3.80/gallon — both numbers written when the MOU was intact and the Strait was reopening. That document is now $16.78/barrel below the current Brent spot price. Every $10 rise in Brent adds roughly 24 cents per gallon to retail gasoline. The $16.78 gap between the EIA Q3 forecast and today's Brent price translates to approximately 40 cents per gallon in additional pump cost over the July forecast baseline — bringing the implied Q3 gasoline price to approximately $4.20/gallon or higher if Brent remains elevated. With Brent at $90+, $4.50 is realistic.
---
| | The IEA's July OMR confirmed global oil supply rebounded by 4.1 mb/d to 98.8 mb/d in June as the ceasefire briefly reopened the Strait — but noted world output remains 9.4 mb/d below pre-war levels, with supply on track to fall 3.7 mb/d in 2026 overall. That rebound is now reversing. The Strait has dropped to three vessels per day. Nine Iranian cities were struck overnight. Iran fired toward the Israeli border. The 4.1 mb/d June rebound was the MOU working for three weeks. The MOU is voided. The August 11 EIA STEO is the next document that will attempt to price this. It will be written against a backdrop of: three dead Americans, nine struck cities, Brent at $90+, a nuclear window with 28 days left, and a Houthi standby order on the last viable bypass route. That is an energy market document nobody in July would have chosen to write.

## Trump Approves Flood Emergency Declaration
President Donald Trump approved a [federal emergency declaration](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAQxvGngc3IHDYmg4cubOnaERl8hpMMRuYSkj59lQxV9-6nv-73fV2Hq6NI2_zpVrT8CGnY8DwiMmMecMU84zY9PU7RZceUNrfvOQ0goRXSCJCDdxSfgyq9HaW_1CXa2nRKK90oXS62Ud0olUclpWp1M3bjOHYGTTCXFgxASfYVkwZkXUuAutJ46WqtO98qPaHWhZLoiVOueEHGhztCfKY75mpKaxntwrwfRfNRQF9Af55nFdLDuNvBtL1OCuhfpgJ6zrd1F2_BHQ_xbokQU_Lilyr-WIW78ZIyfdM2i4CrExkjYSiz9ftJMdLRmkLJeXUU39_w_za8W_gJAAD__134iSw) for 28 flood-stricken Texas counties on Saturday, authorizing FEMA to coordinate disaster relief. The declaration covers counties across South and Central Texas--including Bexar, Kerr, Comal, Bandera, and Uvalde--hit by flooding that began July 12. The federal government will reimburse 75% of eligible emergency response costs, including search and rescue and emergency medical care. Gov. Greg Abbott signed a [disaster declaration Friday in Uvalde,](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uwyAUhZ8Gb0RwDSYeGLqwpWtHi5ibmAobBDd_b1856tC98zn6dM73dZpOPqa4XT_9ipaelzxt-GgJibBOuGK94ja_As7JV08xb76UmicQMHBhOIgp-Jhek-qCPYswyg6tNEelle6V7har0ffqrKSSug_hPJpBX7TqjRI-GBiHLtodJgwIKQWAPGgcj1LrYxiUnlFrpgSGSLkeaEHCp2-X9Mp3rIc5r12yC1FprP9g4Bi4VnCmeltTnn3av-wtBo6ee5hvtPA3g2PixbfMwO0tBm6fwcAJw8DJkYErFVsMuBHfgYW_r9-x_QL46r9z5SE23wgr_yOpqzaUR0wptsEwJa6rj-k9l_4n-W7hJwAA___jd5I2) requesting federal aid. He said the [state had deployed](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAURb_G7rAwAdsUFNu4y7ZbWs_wiNFisOAlTubrR0kxPzD1vffo6vy7LlcIMaTbX9jR0NPnJeFZIxJhWXDHcsNkXw5thAIUcoLjKHkRXAyMj0zwxUGIr0W2zqzc6b5F04-TVFJdpGo342HV2jmQ6PXI3XiRvld2UOs6cS61boN5w_goeN9zIfpOoZ56pSY3SGVRqUZydIFy6WhDwidUH1_5gaWzeW-j2YiO2lz-NGJuxHyeZ_f_CekdNmK2mKhAZJ9dI-ajYA0OEzEq9_1gcKctl_CFlXl0-K4WjAE9g1pDJUgWmc_lB9AW444zxBjqMDaS33YI8fOEfufvYcR3AAAA___cN4fL) more than 2,700 personnel, 90 boats, and 20 aircraft to rescue more than 270 people. FEMA said additional assistance could be approved if damage assessments show more federal aid is warranted.
## Flooding Forces Camp Eagle Evacuation
State troopers and [volunteer firefighters evacuated](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkMGupCAQRb9Gd3QAQX0LFrNx92Y7S1NAoSRIGWC627-ftJk_eNuTk6qT--d7_YaYYt5-w4GmvQOtGV81YWtYVjywbJjd5dElKNAiZTjPQqvkcmR8YpKvHmK6VtV7Y7n_Ej0aMc1KKz0o3e-Gz24KdrDDJEZuvbc2DGIcZ2uFD4MLfTSfY3ySXAgupXho_JqF1rMflXaodac4-tioPNqODd9QQ7roieXh6OiT2Vs7azf86uTSyeWTrypkyI1ypI_zn3ZySeQgdXI5d2pU2SA1c3CcWCrDJ7i_0NCzUOi4MUPYEjJ7sfsr82dlrRDdPhzRs5CIfMxbX4w_XzGlWMepU3w7IKY7r_1s1KeR_wIAAP__QIePNg) about 325 campers from Camp Eagle in Real County on Saturday after flooding washed out the camp's main access road. The Texas Department of Public Safety said Real County Judge Bella Rubio requested the evacuation and that [every camper made it out safely](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkbGu4yAQRb8Gd0R4DBgKim3cvW23tCYwidFiYwEvTv5-5WT_4JX3zOhIV_fP1_yFMcXt_htXcu15y_NGR03UGpWZVip32vwrkE9YsMW84b6XPIMAzcXIQcwBY3rNsgvuKoLtO3L9aKSSapCqW5wBYwxKsIrIWgDptbyq0atee2-BuuhOmRhB9L0A6C-KrOmVMkFL5UkpJgWF2HK5tIUaPbHe0is_qFx8Xrvkltb2yoZfDCYG03Ecl7-0VXVeGUxYWvSJGExnMQZTbdjO-Dbx__ATbinnwGAahOAf4nHdqVROD_Tf2Ci8CSe8J_q88wPrQpXn78bRe6qVl4ynBcaBYxjNYPXApbGaSyTgxmrFvRTXISh9pZvqigv7EVOKVY9MivuKMb27tZ8t8nDwLwAA__8kG54B). Troopers from the DPS South Texas Region worked alongside the Center Point Volunteer Fire Department and local partners. Amphibious SHERP vehicles—one donated to the Center Point firefighters [by Joe Rogan and Ron White](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLtuxCAURL8Gd6wAgx8FRRp3mzaldQ3XNtE1WMC-_j7a5BPSjTTSaM75us5XCBTi9gkH2vpc0xzxUQhrxTzjgXnD6F4eHUGGGlKE88xpVkJ1XPRcidlDoNesG28X4UfZoJX9oI02rTbNbgE6LZxbdIdSo2jHflickqMbhWzXXjXBvsdEr4SUQil5MTgO0pjBd9o4NIZpgT7UlC91x4pPKCu90h3zxaWjIbvXehbWfjA1MTW5pcCt1BDfLVPTG4epiZIDYmr6Tshz2iBynyJU9LzsmE9-xz04Qr4jneh5xuJuyB0cJ0fY6C9iLnxNROkR4sZXSsmHuDXZ-vMRiELpeqbFdkCg32_1f0bvVv0EAAD__8syjb4)—carried campers over the washed-out terrain to buses waiting at the highway. State Rep. Wes Virdell said the campers were never in danger during the severe weather.
## Boxer Hannah Rapp Killed in Crash
Rising professional boxer Hannah "Hanarchy" Rapp, 26, died Saturday after a driver struck her [while she was cycling](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OhCAUxfGnwQ7Dh6hTUGxjN9tuaa5wHcggEGRH3affzL7C1if55eT_dZ_v4IOPj0_YUNdzTXPEYw9YK5YZNywPjOayaAIUqD5FyLmkWTDRUzZQwWYLPlxz11i9MHvjDWo-jJ3qlOxU4_QKduQrjsb0Bq1kbJQS1SpVL-WietZ4_cbYIBjnTAjeKryNXKnR9p0yqBTpGFpfU2mrw4on7Gu40gtLa9LWBO1qzTuRH0RMREzHcbTPpZ7vkYjpbRMxsYGIid-ImBzECI46iFCMu2iBnKlxsGWfIl3SiYU-fQho6VLgJ-3UpO9YL2oK7I6IqSna5sOH4Pd-IB17bODD35X6v4AvLX4DAAD__0MIhOg) on FM 159 in Brazos County. The Brazos County Sheriff's Office said Charles Medina, 31, of Navasota, passed Rapp and another cyclist at a high rate of speed, then braked, reversed, [and accelerated backward](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD0O3CAQRk-DO1YwNv4pKNK427QprVmYNSgYLDxZr28fOVdI9RVPevr0fj2XJ8YU8_oTN7L8fZcl03kkYqa60EZ1pewuTy5hRY4l477XsoCCXqpBglo8xnQtXePtS_lJN2T1MHamM21nmmBbPTnnCLwZ27ebjOv7qX05eI2da1G_m2hvmRpAaa0A9MPQNGpjRt93xpExolPkI5f64EBMXzze6Sofqg9XtibZwLwfov0hYBYwn-f5-H3y94YC5tstYFaDgFlPAuaMHzwKo9wwS6yVDiYvXcC6kpdn5HCTI-GfNTBV6Qk5yFf5UpUBc8ZwD1YXLllx3wXMTbV-P2NK8egH0al1w5j-neP_S_qx8DcAAP__UyWMEg) into her. Medina was charged with manslaughter and is held on a $250,000 bond. Investigators wrote that skid marks and the severity of the vehicle damage contradicted Medina's account that he was backing up slowly. Jail records show it was his 13th booking in Brazos County since 2012. Rapp moved from Indiana to Bryan-College Station about two years ago and fought for a WBC [featherweight world title](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpSAYhZ8GOwwgKLeg2MbubrulAflRsigG_7no20-cV5jmFOckX06-f-_pbWOK-_LXbmDwCnnaoZ4JEKFMsEFZYJ9vD3OyxWLMuz2OkifBRE_ZQAWbvI3pnmTjjWP-xRswfNBSSdVJ1awmBBBBBjvrXmvdyQH6wHsO0jvphqCbaB4YGwTjnAnBWwUvzZXSvpdqBqWIZOAj5tLiCgiXPUO68wdKO-etSWZFPE7S_SFiJGKstbb_HV7PSMT4sIkY2RO8I2J05bY7dfmCQkNcVoz7QqubaQCLK5QKT0lrLslTjJiAnha_irc3EWNTjD9qTCme_UAkWzYb088P_J29jxHfAQAA__8X7IRQ) in June, all while working full-time at Texas A&M.

The Brazos County Sheriff's Office said Charles Medina, 31, of Navasota, passed Rapp and another cyclist at a high rate of speed, then braked, reversed, into her.
